description: Per-execution WebSocket receive-delay measurements: local receive time minus bitFlyer's own exchange execution timestamp, for lightning_executions_FX_BTC_JPY prints. A read-only diagnostic (public channel, no order/private endpoint touched) -- see scripts/measure_ws_latency.py.
source: scripts/measure_ws_latency.py, subscribed to bitFlyer's public WS (wss://ws.lightstream.bitflyer.com/json-rpc, lightning_executions_FX_BTC_JPY) for a fixed measurement window; one row per execution print received.
retention: one file per measurement run/host (this one from the 'vm' host); appended or overwritten depending on how the script is invoked -- not a continuously-running collector, a periodic diagnostic run.

rts.meaning: local (this machine's) receive time when the WS message carrying this execution arrived
rts.tz: UTC (host clock, not NTP-verified by this script)

exec_date.meaning: bitFlyer's own exchange execution time for this print (exec_date field of the lightning_executions message)

delay_s.meaning: rts - exec_date, i.e. how late this machine learned about a trade that already happened
delay_s.notes: contains this host's own clock offset from the exchange -- scripts/measure_ws_latency.py reports that offset separately (HTTP Date header comparison) so it can be subtracted; do not read delay_s as pure network latency

known_defects: delay_s conflates network/processing latency with local clock skew -- see the script's own CLOCK CAVEAT docstring before comparing delay_s across different host runs without also comparing their reported clock offsets
not a continuous feed -- a diagnostic run of a few minutes at a time; large gaps between runs (or between rows within one run, if the process paused) are expected and not a collection failure
